title: fix: restore model filter autocomplete
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Restores the shared editable-combobox dropdown for model search filters.
- Suggests filter names and matching values for the token being typed.
- Keeps selected filters visible while chaining additional filters.
- Matches official publishers such as `publisher:nvidia` and community publishers by public owner.
- Leaves the existing URL-backed search and backend unchanged.

Follow-up to #13996 and #13907.

Tests: focused model-query tests, frontend TypeScript, Biome, production frontend build, and local browser interaction.

gist.headline: Filters find their way home
gist.blurb: The model garden's search box has its little suggestion brain back. Type a filter, pick a publisher, keep chaining—no need to remember the whole taxonomy by hand.
gist.summary: Restored the shared editable-combobox autocomplete for the model search, suggesting filter names and token-matched values while preserving selected filters as users chain queries, including official and community publisher filters such as publisher:nvidia.
gist.impact: Users can again build URL-backed model searches interactively, with autocomplete for publishers and other filters instead of having to type every filter value manually.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model-library garden where Polli is using a glowing retro search terminal whose dropdown sprouts helpful filter tags such as publisher:nvidia; selected tags stay planted in a neat row while new suggestions bloom. Small code-plants and publisher-label seed packets make the restored autocomplete feel like a tool that helps people find the right model without memorizing the whole catalog.
